<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:8pt;">The change in the projected Down 1.00 and 0.50% scenarios at December 31, 2020 compared to December 31, 2019 primarily relates to the significant declines seen in interest rates during 2020. The model assumes a floor on all pertinent market indices of 0.00% except the Federal Funds rate and borrowing rates, which have no assumed floor.<span style="font-size:10pt;"> <br /></span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">29</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="ITEM_6__EXHIBITS"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">C</span><span style="font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">RITICAL ACCOUNTING POLICIES</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management&#8217;s discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations is based upon Capstead&#8217;s consolidated financial statements, which have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States.&#160;&#160;The preparation of these financial statements requires the use of estimates and judgments that can affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities (including contingencies), revenues and expenses, as well as related disclosures.&#160;&#160;These estimates are based on available internal and market information and appropriate valuation methodologies believed to be reasonable under the circumstances, the results of which form the basis for making judgments about the expected useful lives and carrying values of assets and liabilities which can materially affect the determination of net income and book value per common share.&#160;&#160;Actual results may differ from these estimates under different assumptions or conditions.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management believes the following are critical accounting policies in the preparation of Capstead&#8217;s consolidated financial statements that involve the use of estimates requiring considerable judgment:</p>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.85%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-size:11pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:11pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;">Amortization of investment premiums on residential mortgage investments&#160;</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;">&#8211;&#160;Investment premiums on residential mortgage investments are recognized in earnings as adjustments to interest income by the interest method over the estimated lives of the related assets.&#160;&#160;Amortization is affected by actual portfolio runoff (scheduled and unscheduled principal paydowns) and by estimates and judgments related to future levels of mortgage prepayments that may be necessary to achieve the required effective yield over the estimated life of the related investment.</span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.85%;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Mortgage prepayment expectations can change based on how current and projected changes in interest rates impact the economic attractiveness of mortgage refinance opportunities, if available, and other factors such as lending industry underwriting practices and capacity constraints, regulatory changes, borrower credit profiles and the health of the economy and housing markets.&#160;&#160;Management estimates future mortgage prepayments based on these factors and past experiences with specific investments within the portfolio.&#160;&#160;Should actual prepayment rates differ materially from these estimates, investment premiums would be expensed at a different pace.</p>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.85%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-size:11pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:11pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;">Fair value and impairment accounting for residential mortgage investments&#160;</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;">&#8211;&#160;Nearly all of Capstead&#8217;s residential mortgage investments are held in the form of mortgage securities that are classified as available-for-sale and recorded at fair value on the balance sheet with unrealized gains and losses recorded in </span><span style="font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;">Stockholders&#8217; equity</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;"> as a component of </span><span style="font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;">Accumulated other comprehensive income</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;">.&#160;&#160;Fair values fluctuate with current and projected changes in interest rates, prepayment expectations and other factors such as market liquidity conditions and the perceived credit quality of Agency Securities.&#160;&#160;Judgment is required to interpret market data and develop estimated fair values, particularly in circumstances of deteriorating credit quality and market liquidity.&#160;&#160;See NOTE&#160;8 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for discussion of how Capstead values its residential mortgage investments.</span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.85%;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Generally, gains or losses are recognized in earnings only if securities are sold&#59; however, if a decline in fair value of a mortgage security below its amortized cost occurs, the difference between amortized cost and fair value would be recognized in earnings as a component of <span style="font-style:italic;">Other (expense) income</span> if the decline was credit-related or it was determined to be more likely than not that the Company will incur a loss via an asset sale.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">30</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.85%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-size:11pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:11pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-size:11pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"></span><span style="font-size:11pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"></span><span style="font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;">Accounting for derivative instruments&#160;</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;">&#8211;&#160;Derivatives are recorded as assets or liabilities and carried at fair value.&#160;&#160;Fair values fluctuate with current and projected changes in interest rates and other factors such as the Company&#8217;s and its counterparties&#8217; nonperformance risk.&#160;&#160;Judgment is required to develop estimated fair values.</span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.85%;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The accounting for changes in fair value of each derivative held depends on whether it has been designated as an accounting hedge, as well as the type of hedging relationship identified.&#160;&#160;To qualify as a cash flow hedge for accounting purposes, at the inception of the hedge relationship the Company must anticipate and document that the hedge relationship will be highly effective and must monitor ongoing effectiveness on at least a quarterly basis.&#160;&#160;As long as the hedge relationship remains highly effective, changes in fair value of the derivative are recorded in <span style="font-style:italic;">Accumulated other comprehensive income.</span>&#160;&#160;Changes in fair value of derivatives not held as accounting hedges, or for which the hedge relationship is deemed to no longer be highly effective and as a result hedge accounting is terminated, are recorded in earnings as a component of <span style="font-style:italic;">Other (expense) income.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.85%;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="CriticalAccountingPoliciesEnd">The Company uses derivatives primarily in the form of interest rate swap agreements to hedge the variability in borrowing rates on its secured borrowings and unsecured borrowings.&#160;&#160;For derivatives designated as accounting hedges, fixed interest payments and variable interest receipts are recorded as an adjustment to interest expense on the related designated borrowings. For derivatives not designated as accounting hedges, fixed interest payments and variable interest receipts are recorded as a component of <span style="font-style:italic;">Other (expense) income. </span>For derivatives initially designated as an accounting hedge and subsequently de-designated, any unrealized gain or loss included in <span style="font-style:italic;">Accumulated other comprehensive income </span>at the time of de-designation is amortized as an adjustment to interest expense on the related borrowings over the remaining term of the derivatives.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;Financial Condition &#8211; Residential Mortgage Investments&#8221; and NOTE 6 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information regarding the Company&#8217;s current use of derivatives and its related risk management policies.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">31</p>

<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:bold;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:11pt;" id="ITEM_8_FINANCIAL_STATEMENTS_SUPPLEMENTAR">FINANCIAL STATEMENTS AND SUPPLEMENTARY DATA</p></td></tr></table></div>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>

<td valign="top" style="width:94.72%;">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:0.98%;">

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">All financial statement schedules are omitted because they are not applicable or the required information is included in the consolidated financial statements and notes thereto.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Financial statements of subsidiaries have been omitted as such entities do not individually or in the aggregate exceed the 20% threshold under either the investment or income tests applicable under the appropriate regulations for inclusion.&#160;&#160;The Company owned 100% of each of its subsidiaries.<br /></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">32</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="REPORT_INDEPENDENT_REGISTERED_PUBLIC_ACC">Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">To the Shareholders and the Board of Directors of Capstead Mortgage Corporation</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Opinion on the Financial Statements </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:11pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Capstead Mortgage Corporation (the Company) as of December 31, 2020 and 2019, the related consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive income (loss), stockholders' equity and cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2020, and the related notes (collectively referred to as the &#8220;consolidated financial statements&#8221;). In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company at December 31, 2020 and 2019, and the results of its operations and its cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2020, in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:11pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (PCAOB), the Company's internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2020, based on criteria established in Internal Control-Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013 framework) and our report dated February 19, 2021 expressed an unqualified opinion thereon. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Basis for Opinion </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:11pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">These financial statements are the responsibility of the Company's management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company&#8217;s financial statements based on our audits. We are a public accounting firm registered with the PCAOB and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:11pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud. Our audits included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. Our audits also included evaluating the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the financial statements. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:11pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Critical Audit Matter</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:11pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The critical audit matter communicated below is a matter arising from the current period audit of the financial statements that was communicated or required to be communicated to the audit committee and that: (1) relate to accounts or disclosures that are material to the financial statements and (2) involved our especially challenging, subjective or complex judgments. The communication of a critical audit matter does not alter in any way our opinion on the consolidated financial statements, taken as a whole, and we are not, by communicating the critical audit matter below, providing a separate opinion on the critical audit matter or on the accounts or disclosures to which it relates. </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">33</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:11pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Residential mortgage investments &#8211; Debt Securities</span></p>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:99.89%;">
<tr>
<td style="width:18.22%;"></td>
<td style="width:81.68%;"></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-bottom:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Description of the Matter</p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Residential mortgage investments totaled $7.94 billion at December 31, 2020, consisting of Agency Securities classified as available-for-sale.&#160;&#160;As explained in Note 2 and Note 8 of the consolidated financial statements, residential mortgage investments are carried at fair value at each reporting date with unrealized gains and losses reported as a separate component of Accumulated other comprehensive income (loss). Fair values are influenced by current and projected changes in interest rates, prepayment expectations, market liquidity conditions and other factors including consideration of recent trading activity for similar investments and pricing levels. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Auditing the Company&#8217;s accounting for certain securities within its residential mortgage investments portfolio was complex due to the estimation uncertainty in determining the fair value as these securities, which represent 1.95% of the portfolio of Residential mortgage investments, tend to have higher uncertainty in prepayment expectations, less recent trading activity or variability in pricing levels. </p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-bottom:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">How We Addressed the Matter in Our Audit</p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We evaluated and tested the design and operating effectiveness of controls addressing the identified risks related to the Company&#8217;s process used in determining the valuation of residential mortgage investments, including management&#8217;s review of available third-party pricing data. We also tested management&#8217;s controls over the completeness and accuracy of the data used in the valuation. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our audit procedures included, among others, independently pricing a sample of these securities which involved internally developing fair value estimates using independently derived data for significant assumptions (e.g. prepayment rate and portfolio yield) to compare with management&#8217;s determined prices. We involved an internal valuation specialist and third-party data in our procedures. Additionally, we performed analytical procedures, which included a sensitivity analysis to understand the impact of a change in average fair value compared to management&#8217;s mark-to-market adjustment for these securities.&#160;&#160;</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-bottom:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-bottom:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-bottom:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-bottom:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p></td>

<p style="margin-top:3pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:8pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">See accompanying Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">39</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:13.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-variant: small-caps;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;" id="NOTES_TO_CONSOLIDATED_FINANCIAL_STATEMEN"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-size:13.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-variant: small-caps;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;">Notes to Consolidated</span><span style="font-weight:bold;font-size:13.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-variant: small-caps;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;"> Financial Statements</span></p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000317" name="us-gaap:NatureOfOperations" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 1 &#8212; BUSINESS</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Capstead Mortgage Corporation operates as a self-managed real estate investment trust for federal income tax purposes (a &#8220;REIT&#8221;) and is based in Dallas, Texas.&#160;&#160;Unless the context otherwise indicates, Capstead Mortgage Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, is referred to as &#8220;Capstead&#8221; or the &#8220;Company.&#8221;&#160;&#160;Capstead earns income from investing in a leveraged portfolio of residential mortgage pass-through securities currently consisting primarily of adjustable-rate mortgage (&#8220;ARM&#8221;) securities issued and guaranteed by government-sponsored enterprises, either Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, or by an agency of the federal government, Ginnie Mae. Together, these securities are referred to as &#8220;Agency Securities&#8221; and are considered to have limited, if any, credit risk.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000318" name="us-gaap:SignificantAccountingPoliciesTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000318_dcnt_37d6ae7c-8d02-4532-b181-7f8515c063ce">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 2 &#8212; ACCOUNTING POLICIES</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000329" name="us-gaap:BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Basis of Presentation</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Capstead Mortgage Corporation and its wholly-owned and majority-owned subsidiaries over which it exercises control.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to variable interest entity (&#8220;VIE&#8221;) accounting principles, Capstead considers for consolidation any VIE in which it holds an interest.&#160;&#160;Intercompany balances and transactions are eliminated.&#160;&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000330" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In June 2016, Accounting Standards Update No. 2016-13, Financial Instruments &#8211; Credit Losses (&#8220;ASU 2016-13&#8221;) was issued which replaced the incurred loss impairment methodology in previous GAAP with a methodology that is designed to better reflect expected credit losses. For financial instruments carried at amortized cost, impairment is measured as a current estimate of expected lifetime credit losses. For available-for-sale debt securities in which changes in fair value are recorded in accumulated other comprehensive income, the write-down of available-for-sale securities under the &#8220;other-than-temporarily&#8221; impaired model was replaced with an allowance for credit losses model. ASU 2016-13 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2019 and interim periods within those fiscal years. The Company adopted ASU 2016-13 on January 1, 2020 which had no material effect on the Company&#8217;s results of operations, financial condition and cash flows primarily due to the limited, if any, credit risk of Agency Securities.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000331" name="us-gaap:UseOfEstimates" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Use of Estimates</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fair values of nearly all financial instruments held by the Company are estimated based on a market approach using available market information and appropriate valuation methodologies (Level Two Inputs)&#59; however, judgment is required in interpreting market data to develop these estimates.&#160;&#160;Fair values fluctuate on a daily basis and are influenced by changes in, and market expectations for changes in, interest rates, market liquidity conditions and levels of mortgage prepayments, as well as other factors.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, estimates of fair value are as of the balance sheet dates and are not necessarily indicative of the amounts that could be realized in a current market exchange.&#160;&#160;The use of different market assumptions and estimation methodologies may have a material effect on estimated fair values.&#160;&#160;Judgment is also exercised in making impairment conclusions and estimating impairment charges.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Amortization of investment premiums on financial assets is based in part on estimates of future levels of mortgage prepayments. Estimates are influenced by changes in, and market expectations for changes in, interest rates, market liquidity conditions, actual levels of mortgage prepayments and other factors.&#160;&#160;Judgment is required in developing these estimates, however the actual level of mortgage prepayments for a given accounting period is the single largest determinant in amortizing investment premiums.</p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">40</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000318_dcnt_37d6ae7c-8d02-4532-b181-7f8515c063ce" continuedAt="F_000318_dcnt_bc954e66-870f-4352-bcfc-1beec0915d6d"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000332" name="us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cash and Cash Equivalents</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cash and cash equivalents<span style="font-style:normal;"> include unrestricted cash on hand and highly liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less when purchased.</span></p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000333" name="cmo:FinancialAssetsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Financial Assets</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Capstead&#8217;s financial assets consist of Agency Securities classified as available-for-sale and carried at fair value with net unrealized gains and losses reported as a separate component of <span style="font-style:italic;">Accumulated other comprehensive income</span>.&#160;&#160;Interest is recorded as income when earned.&#160;&#160;Investment premiums and discounts are recognized as adjustments to interest income by the interest method over the expected life of the related financial assets.&#160;&#160;Realized gains and losses from any financial asset sales are recorded as a component of <span style="font-style:italic;">Other (expense) income</span>.&#160;&#160;The specific identification method is used to determine the cost of financial assets sold. Financial assets are reviewed for potential impairment at each balance sheet date.&#160;&#160;Impairments of investments in mortgage securities can occur with changes in the Company&#8217;s intent or ability to hold the mortgage securities until any declines in fair value are recovered and as a result of adverse changes in the financial condition of the issuer(s) such that a full recovery of cost basis is no longer expected.&#160;&#160;The amount of any such impairment is measured by comparing the recorded amount of the security to its fair value.&#160;&#160;If the decline in fair value is credit-related, an allowance for credit losses would be recognized in earnings as a component of <span style="font-style:italic;">Other (expense) income. </span>If it was determined to be more likely than not that the Company will incur a loss via an asset sale, the difference between amortized cost and fair value would be recognized in earnings as a component of <span style="font-style:italic;">Other (expense) income.</span></p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000334" name="us-gaap:DebtPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Borrowings</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Secured borrowings in the form of repurchase arrangements create exposure to the potential for failure on the part of counterparties to honor their commitment to return pledged collateral.&#160;&#160;In the event of a default by a repurchase arrangement counterparty, the Company may have difficulty recovering its collateral.&#160;&#160;To mitigate this risk, the Company monitors the creditworthiness of its counterparties and manages its exposure to any single counterparty.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Capstead&#8217;s borrowings are carried at their principal balances outstanding net of related debt issuance costs and debt discounts, if applicable.&#160;&#160;Debt issuance costs associated with <span style="font-style:italic;">Unsecured borrowings</span> are recognized as adjustments to interest expense by the interest method over the term of these borrowings.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000335" name="us-gaap:DerivativesReportingOfDerivativeActivity" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000335_dcnt_12768e85-1703-4782-9e5f-d7a42ce3703c">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Derivative Financial Instruments (&#8220;Derivatives&#8221;)</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Derivatives used by Capstead for risk management purposes are carried at fair value as assets or liabilities.&#160;&#160;The accounting for changes in fair value of Derivatives held depends on whether it has been designated as a hedge for accounting purposes, as well as the type of hedging relationship identified.&#160;&#160;Capstead may designate any Derivatives held as cash flow hedges related to a designated portion of its current and anticipated future borrowings.&#160;&#160;To qualify as a cash flow hedge, at the inception of the hedge relationship the Company must document that the hedge relationship is anticipated to be highly effective and monitor ongoing effectiveness on at least a quarterly basis.&#160;&#160;As long as the hedge relationship remains effective, the change in fair value of the Derivatives are recorded in <span style="font-style:italic;">Accumulated other comprehensive income</span>.&#160;&#160;Changes in fair value of Derivatives not held as accounting hedges, if any, or for which the hedge relationship is no longer considered highly effective, are recorded in earnings as a component of <span style="font-style:italic;">Other (expense) income. </span>On March 1, 2019 the Company discontinued its use of hedge accounting on its interest rate swaps related to <span style="font-style:italic;">Secured borrowings</span>, while retaining hedge accounting for swaps related to <span style="font-style:italic;">Unsecured borrowings</span>.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company uses Derivatives primarily in the form of interest rate swap agreements to hedge the variability in borrowing rates on its secured and unsecured borrowings. If designated as accounting hedges, related fixed interest payments and variable interest receipts are recorded as an adjustment to interest expense on the related designated borrowings. If not designated as accounting hedges, fixed </p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">41</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000318_dcnt_bc954e66-870f-4352-bcfc-1beec0915d6d" continuedAt="F_000318_dcnt_d6682708-a257-4c6d-b59f-75e949c75b45"><ix:continuation id="F_000335_dcnt_12768e85-1703-4782-9e5f-d7a42ce3703c">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">interest payments and variable interest receipts are recorded as a component of </span><span style="font-style:italic;">Other (expense) income</span><span style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">. For </span><span style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">D</span><span style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">erivatives initially designated as accounting hedge</span><span style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">s</span><span style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> and subsequently de-designated, unrealized gain or loss included in </span><span style="font-style:italic;">Accumulated other comprehensive income</span><span style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> at the time of de-designation is amortized as an adjustment to interest expense on the related borrowings over the remaining term of the </span><span style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">D</span><span style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">erivatives.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Derivatives create exposure to credit risk related to the potential for failure on the part of counterparties to honor their commitments.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Company is required to post collateral primarily based on any declines in the market value of the Derivatives.&#160;&#160;In the event of default by a counterparty, the Company may have difficulty recovering its collateral and may not receive payments provided for under the terms of the Derivatives.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to regulatory changes implemented in 2013, most Derivatives held at December&#160;31, 2020 were entered into through Derivative exchanges established in part to mitigate credit risk.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cash collateral receivable from derivative counterparties<span style="font-style:normal;">, when present, represents cash remitted to swap counterparties to meet initial and ongoing margin requirements that are based on the fair value of these Derivatives, including related interest receivable or payable under the terms of the agreements.&#160;&#160;The Company may also remit mortgage securities to certain of its swap counterparties to meet ongoing margin requirements.&#160;&#160;Such mortgage securities, if any, are included in </span>Residential mortgage investments.&#160;&#160;<span style="font-style:normal;">Similarly,</span> Cash collateral payable to derivative counterparties<span style="font-style:normal;">, when present, represents cash received from counterparties to meet margin call requirements.&#160;&#160;For presentation purposes, the Company does not offset individual counterparty collateral receivables (or payables) with the recorded fair value of related interest rate swap agreements pursuant to master netting arrangements.&#160;&#160;In addition, gross unrealized gains on Derivatives (recorded as assets) are stated separately from gross unrealized losses (recorded as liabilities) without regard to counterparty.&#160;&#160;Certain cash margin amounts are presented on a net basis against the fair value of related Derivatives.</span></p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000336" name="us-gaap:CompensationRelatedCostsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Long-term Incentive Compensation</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Capstead provides its employees and its directors with long-term incentive compensation in the form of equity-based awards.&#160;&#160;Equity-based compensation costs are initially measured at the estimated fair value of the awards on the grant date developed using appropriate valuation methodologies.&#160;&#160;Valuation methodologies used and subsequent expense recognition is dependent upon each award&#8217;s service and performance conditions, the latter also referred to as performance metrics. Capstead has elected not to estimate future award forfeitures when valuing equity-based awards and adjusts compensation costs as actual forfeitures occur.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Compensation costs for equity-based awards subject only to service conditions are measured at the closing stock price on the dates of grant and are recognized as expense on a straight-line basis over the requisite service periods for the awards, as adjusted for any forfeitures.&#160;&#160;Compensation costs for components of equity-based awards subject to nonmarket-based performance metrics (i.e. metrics not predicated on changes in the Company&#8217;s stock price), are measured at the closing stock price on the dates of grant, adjusted for the probability of achieving benchmarks included in the performance metrics.&#160;&#160;These initial cost estimates are recognized as expense over the requisite performance periods, adjusted for subsequent changes in performance estimates.&#160;&#160;Compensation costs for components of equity-based awards subject to market-based performance metrics are measured at the dates of grant using Monte Carlo simulations which incorporate into the valuations the inherent uncertainty regarding achieving the market-based performance metrics.&#160;&#160;These initial valuation amounts are recognized as expense over the requisite performance periods, subject to adjustments only for actual forfeitures.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000337" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000337_dcnt_e54c1f96-ff13-4c3c-a3b2-aeb465ed672c">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Income Taxes</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Capstead Mortgage Corporation and its qualified REIT subsidiaries have elected to be taxed as a REIT.&#160;&#160;As a result, Capstead is not taxed on taxable income distributed to stockholders if certain REIT qualification tests are met.&#160;&#160;Capstead&#8217;s policy is to distribute <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000355" name="cmo:PercentageOfTaxableIncomeToBeDistributed" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">100</ix:nonFraction>% of its taxable income, after application of available tax attributes, within the time limits prescribed by the Internal Revenue Code (the &#8220;Code&#8221;), which may extend into the subsequent taxable year.&#160;&#160;The Company may find it advantageous from time to </p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">42</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000318_dcnt_d6682708-a257-4c6d-b59f-75e949c75b45"><ix:continuation id="F_000337_dcnt_e54c1f96-ff13-4c3c-a3b2-aeb465ed672c">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">time to elect taxable REIT subsidiary status for certain of its subsidiaries in which case taxable income of any such subsidiary would be subject to federal and, where applicable, state or local income taxes.&#160;&#160;Any such income taxes are accounted for using the liability method.&#160;&#160;Related deferred income tax assets and liabilities are determined based on differences between the financial reporting and tax bases of assets and liabilities and are measured using enacted tax rates and laws that will be in effect when the differences are expected to reverse.&#160;&#160;The Company has not recognized any liabilities for unrecognized tax benefits using a &#8220;more likely than not&#8221; threshold for the recognition and measurement of the financial statement effects of tax positions taken on a tax return filing.&#160;&#160;Should any such liabilities be recognized in future periods, the Company will record related interest and penalties in </span><span style="font-style:italic;">Other </span><span style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">g</span><span style="font-style:italic;">eneral and administrative expense</span><span style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">.</span></p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000338" name="cmo:DividendClassificationPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Dividend Classification</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The tax and financial reporting classification of dividends can differ primarily as a result of differences between taxable income attributable to a particular tax year and that year&#8217;s <span style="font-style:italic;">Net income (loss)</span>, the amount and timing of dividends paid relative to taxable income and how such taxable income is allocated to dividends paid.</p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">43</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000319" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerShareTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 3 &#8212; NET INCOME (LOSS) PER COMMON SHARE</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Basic net income (loss) per common share is computed by dividing net (loss) income, after deducting dividends paid or accrued on preferred stock and allocating earnings to equity awards deemed to be participating securities pursuant to the two-class method, by the average number of shares of common stock outstanding, calculated excluding unvested stock awards.&#160;&#160;Participating securities include unvested equity awards that contain non-forfeitable rights to dividends prior to vesting.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Diluted net income (loss) per common share is computed by dividing the numerator used to compute basic net income (loss) per common share by the denominator used to compute basic net income (loss) per common share, further adjusted for the dilutive effect, if any, of equity awards and shares of preferred stock when and if convertible into shares of common stock.&#160;&#160;Shares of the Company&#8217;s <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000356" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockDividendRatePercentage" contextRef="C_0000766701_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapSeriesEPreferredStockMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">7.50</ix:nonFraction>% Series E Cumulative Redeemable Preferred Stock are contingently convertible into shares of common stock only upon the occurrence of a change in control and subject to the conditions set forth in our charter and therefore are not considered dilutive securities absent such an occurrence.&#160;&#160;Any unvested equity awards that are deemed participating securities are included in the calculation of diluted net income (loss) per common share, if dilutive, under either the two-class method or the treasury stock method, depending upon which method produces the more dilutive result.&#160;&#160;<ix:nonNumeric id="F_000339" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfEarningsPerShareBasicAndDilutedTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000339_cnt_1">The following table illustrates the computation of basic and diluted net income (loss) per common share for the indicated periods (dollars in thousands, except per share amounts).&#160;</ix:nonNumeric></p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Agency Securities are considered to have limited, if any, credit risk because the timely payment of principal and interest is guaranteed. The maturity of Agency Securities is directly affected by prepayments of principal on the underlying mortgage loans.&#160;&#160;Consequently, actual maturities will be significantly shorter than the portfolio&#8217;s weighted average contractual maturity of 292 months.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Capstead&#8217;s ARM Agency Securities are backed by residential mortgage loans that have coupon interest rates that adjust at least annually to more current interest rates or begin doing so after an initial fixed-rate period.&#160;&#160;After the initial fixed-rate period, if applicable, mortgage loans underlying ARM securities typically either (i) adjust annually based on specified margins over the one-year London interbank offered rate (&#8220;LIBOR&#8221;) or the one-year Constant Maturity U.S. Treasury Note Rate (&#8220;CMT&#8221;), (ii) adjust semiannually based on specified margins over six-month LIBOR, or (iii) adjust monthly based on specified margins over indices such as one-month LIBOR, the Eleventh District Federal Reserve Bank Cost of Funds Index, or over a rolling twelve month average of the one-year CMT index, usually subject to periodic and lifetime limits, or caps, on the amount of such adjustments during any single interest rate adjustment period and over the contractual term of the underlying loans.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Capstead classifies its ARM investments based on average number of months until coupon reset (&#8220;months to roll&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Months to roll is an indicator of asset duration which is a measure of market price sensitivity to interest rate movements.&#160;&#160;A shorter duration generally indicates less interest rate risk.&#160;&#160;Current-reset ARM investments have months to <p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000321" name="cmo:PortfolioRelatedSecuredBorrowingsDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000321_dcnt_be873c94-d641-41f1-9ac3-af7590b082ef">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 5 &#8212; SECURED BORROWINGS</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Capstead pledges its <span style="font-style:italic;">Residential mortgage investments</span> as collateral for secured borrowings primarily in the form of repurchase arrangements with commercial banks and other financial institutions.&#160;&#160;Repurchase arrangements entered into by the Company involve the sale and a simultaneous agreement to repurchase the transferred assets at a future date and are accounted for as financings.&#160;&#160;The Company maintains the beneficial interest in the specific securities pledged during the term of each repurchase arrangement and receives the related principal and interest payments.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The terms and conditions of secured borrowings are negotiated on a transaction-by-transaction basis when each such borrowing is initiated or renewed.&#160;&#160;The amount borrowed is generally equal to the fair value of the securities pledged, as determined by the lending counterparty, less an agreed-upon discount, referred to as a &#8220;haircut.&#8221;&#160;&#160;Interest rates are generally fixed based on prevailing rates corresponding to the terms of the borrowings. Interest may be paid monthly or at the termination of a borrowing at which time the Company may enter into a new borrowing at prevailing haircuts and rates with the same lending counterparty or repay that counterparty and negotiate financing with a different lending counterparty.&#160;&#160;None of the Company&#8217;s lending counterparties are obligated to renew or otherwise enter into new borrowings at the conclusion of existing borrowings.&#160;&#160;In response to declines in fair value of pledged securities due to changes in market conditions or the publishing of monthly security pay-down factors, lending counterparties typically require the Company to post additional securities as collateral, pay down borrowings or fund cash margin accounts with the counterparties in order to re-establish the agreed-upon collateral requirements.&#160;&#160;These actions are referred to as margin calls.&#160;&#160;Conversely, in response to increases in fair value of pledged securities, the Company routinely margin calls its lending counterparties in order to have previously pledged collateral returned.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">46</p>

<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">47</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000323" name="us-gaap:DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000323_dcnt_3ea472fa-c32d-422f-8959-e193d8939350">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="NOTE_7_USE_DERIVATIVES_FSETTING_DISCLOSU">NOTE 6 &#8212; USE OF DERIVATIVES, OFFSETTING DISCLOSURES AND CHANGES IN OTHER COMPREHENSIVE INCOME BY COMPONENT</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Capstead&#8217;s portfolio of Derivatives hedge the variability of the underlying benchmark interest rate of current and forecasted 30- to 90-day secured borrowings. The Company attempts to mitigate exposure to higher interest rates primarily by entering into pay-fixed, receive-variable, interest rate swap agreements for terms between <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000480" name="us-gaap:DerivativeTermOfContract" contextRef="C_0000766701_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapDerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_us-gaapInterestRateSwapMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">eighteen months</ix:nonNumeric> and <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000481" name="us-gaap:DerivativeTermOfContract" contextRef="C_0000766701_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapDerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_us-gaapInterestRateSwapMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">three years</ix:nonNumeric>. From an economic perspective, this hedge relationship establishes a relatively stable fixed rate on related borrowings because the variable-rate payments received on the swap agreements offset a significant portion of the interest accruing on the borrowings, leaving the fixed-rate swap payments as the Company&#8217;s effective borrowing rate, subject to certain adjustments. Additionally, changes in fair value of these Derivatives tend to offset opposing changes in fair value of the Company&#8217;s residential mortgage investments that can occur in response to changes in market interest rates.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company discontinued hedge accounting in March 2019 for its secured borrowings-related interest rate swaps and, for GAAP purposes, related changes in fair value are recorded in the Company&#8217;s consolidated statements of operations beginning on the de-designation date. Also, for GAAP purposes related net unrealized gains recorded in <span style="font-style:italic;">Accumulated other comprehensive income </span>through the de-designation date are being recognized as a component of interest expense in the Company&#8217;s consolidated statements of operations over the contractual terms of these swaps. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During 2020 Capstead entered into swap agreements with notional amounts totaling $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000482" name="cmo:SwapAgreementNotionalAmountDuringPeriod" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" decimals="-7" scale="9">5.77</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion requiring fixed-rate interest payments averaging <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000483" name="cmo:SwapAgreementAverageInterestRateDuringPeriod" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" decimals="4" scale="-2">0.57</ix:nonFraction>% for periods between eighteen months and three years commencing on various dates between January 2020 and December 2020. During 2020, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000486" name="cmo:SwapAgreementNotionalAmountExpiringDuringPeriod" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" decimals="-6" scale="6">800</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million notional amount of swaps requiring fixed-rate interest payments averaging <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000487" name="cmo:SwapAgreementAverageInterestRateExpiringDuringPeriod" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" decimals="4" scale="-2">2.20</ix:nonFraction>% matured.&#160;&#160;The Company also terminated $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000484" name="cmo:SwapAgreementTerminatedNotionalAmountDuringPeriod" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" decimals="-7" scale="9">9.40</ix:nonFraction> billion notional amount of swaps requiring fixed-rate interest payments averaging <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000485" name="cmo:SwapAgreementTerminatedAverageInterestRateDuringPeriod" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" decimals="4" scale="-2">1.54</ix:nonFraction>% during 2020. <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000342" name="cmo:ScheduleOfDerivativeAgreementExpirationPeriodAndTheirCharacteristicsTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0000766701_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000342_cnt_1">At December&#160;31, 2020, the Company&#8217;s portfolio financing-related swap positions, all of which were either SOFR- or OIS-indexed, had the following characteristics (dollars in thousands):</ix:nonNumeric></p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has three-month LIBOR-indexed, pay-fixed, receive-variable, interest rate swap agreements with notional amounts totaling $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000499" name="cmo:SwapAgreementNotionalAmountDuringPeriod" contextRef="C_0000766701_20100101_20101231" decimals="-6" scale="6">100</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and average fixed rates of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000500" name="cmo:SwapAgreementAverageInterestRateDuringPeriod" contextRef="C_0000766701_20100101_20101231" decimals="4" scale="-2">4.09</ix:nonFraction>% with <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000501" name="us-gaap:DerivativeTermOfContract" contextRef="C_0000766701_us-gaapDerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_us-gaapInterestRateSwapMember_20100101_20101231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">20</ix:nonNumeric>-year payment terms coinciding with the floating-rate terms of the Company&#8217;s <span style="font-style:italic;">Unsecured borrowings </span>that mature in 2035 and 2036. These Derivatives, which are designated as cash flow hedges for accounting purposes, hedge the variability of the underlying benchmark interest rate associated with the floating-rate terms of these long-term borrowings. These Derivatives&#8217; LIBOR-indexed receive rates match the underlying floating-rate terms of the Company&#8217;s <span style="font-style:italic;">Unsecured borrowings</span> and therefore the eventual replacement of the LIBOR index on these Derivatives is not expected to have any financial impact.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Interest rate swap agreements are measured at fair value on a recurring basis primarily using Level Two Inputs in accordance with ASU 2010-06, <span style="font-style:italic;">Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures</span> <span style="font-style:italic;">(Topic 820)</span>.&#160;&#160;In determining fair value estimates for swaps, Capstead utilizes the standard methodology of netting the discounted future fixed cash payments and the discounted future variable cash receipts which are based on expected future interest rates derived from observable market interest rate curves. Eurodollar futures are measured at fair value using Level 1 inputs based on quoted exchange prices on these contracts.&#160;&#160; The </p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">48</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000323_dcnt_3ea472fa-c32d-422f-8959-e193d8939350" continuedAt="F_000323_dcnt_0fff2b25-b79c-4516-bf57-60d92a9bd0a5">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Company also incorporates both its own nonperformance risk and its counterparties&#8217; nonperformance risk in determining fair value.&#160;&#160;In considering the effect of nonperformance risk, the Company considered the impact of netting and credit enhancements, such as collateral postings and guarantees, and has concluded that counterparty risk is not significant to the overall valuation.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair value of exchange-traded swap agreements hedging <span style="font-style:italic;">Secured borrowings </span>is calculated including accrued interest and net of variation margin amounts received or paid through the exchange, resulting in separately presenting on the balance sheet a fair value amount representing the unsettled fair value of these Derivatives. Non-exchange traded swap agreements held as cash flow hedges of <span style="font-style:italic;">Unsecured borrowings </span>are reported at fair value calculated excluding accrued interest. At December&#160;31, 2020, <span style="font-style:italic;">Cash collateral receivable from derivative counterparties </span>includes initial margin for all Derivatives and variation margin for non-exchange traded Derivatives. <p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 8 &#8212; FAIR VALUES OF FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair value of Capstead&#8217;s financial assets and liabilities are influenced by changes in, and market expectations for changes in, interest rates and market liquidity conditions, as well as other factors beyond the control of management. With the exception of the fair value of Eurodollar futures, all fair values were determined using Level 2 Inputs in accordance with ASU 2010-06, Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures (Topic 820). Eurodollar futures are Derivatives for which Level 1 inputs are used to determine fair value. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Residential mortgage investments, all of which are mortgage securities classified as available-for-sale, are measured at fair value on a recurring basis. In determining fair value estimates the Company considers recent trading activity for similar investments and pricing levels indicated by lenders in connection with designating collateral for secured borrowings, provided such pricing levels are considered indicative of actual market clearing transactions. The Company currently bases fair value for <span style="font-style:italic;">Unsecured borrowings</span> on discounted cash flows using Company estimates for market yields. Excluded from these disclosures are financial instruments for which cost basis is deemed to approximate fair value due primarily to the short duration of these instruments, which are valued using primarily Level 1 measurements, including <span style="font-style:italic;">Cash and cash equivalents</span>, <span style="font-style:italic;">Cash collateral receivable</span> <span style="font-style:italic;">from derivative counterparties</span>, receivables, payables and <span style="font-style:italic;">Secured borrowings</span> with initial terms of <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000673" name="cmo:InvestmentRepurchaseAgreementInitialTerm" contextRef="C_0000766701_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durday">120</ix:nonNumeric> days or less. See NOTE 6 for information relative to the valuation of interest rate swap agreements.</p>
